_about: The Latin Vulgate (Clementine, 1592) and the Douay-Rheims English made from it (Challoner, 1750), public domain, under the Vulgate’s own verse numbers. Jerome made his Tobit in one day from an Aramaic copy, and its verses do not line up with the Greek.

vulgate.1:1: Tobias ex tribu et civitate Nephthali (quæ est in superioribus Galilææ supra Naasson, post viam quæ ducit ad occidentem, in sinistro habens civitatem Sephet)
vulgate.1:2: cum captus esset in diebus Salmanasar regis Assyriorum, in captivitate tamen positus, viam veritatis non deseruit,
vulgate.1:3: ita ut omnia quæ habere poterat, quotidie concaptivis fratribus, qui erant ex ejus genere, impertiret.
vulgate.1:4: Cumque esset junior omnibus in tribu Nephthali, nihil tamen puerile gessit in opere.
vulgate.1:5: Denique, cum irent omnes ad vitulos aureos quos Jeroboam fecerat rex Israël, hic solus fugiebat consortia omnium.
vulgate.1:6: Sed pergebat in Jerusalem ad templum Domini, et ibi adorabat Dominum Deum Israël, omnia primitiva sua et decimas suas fideliter offerens,
vulgate.1:7: ita ut in tertio anno proselytis et advenis ministraret omnem decimationem.
vulgate.1:8: Hæc et his similia secundum legem Dei puerulus observabat.
vulgate.1:9: Cum vero factus esset vir, accepit uxorem Annam de tribu sua, genuitque ex ea filium, nomen suum imponens ei:
vulgate.1:10: quem ab infantia timere Deum docuit, et abstinere ab omni peccato.
vulgate.1:11: Igitur, cum per captivitatem devenisset cum uxore sua et filio in civitatem Niniven cum omni tribu sua
vulgate.1:12: (cum omnes ederent ex cibis gentilium), iste custodivit animam suam, et numquam contaminatus est in escis eorum.
vulgate.1:13: Et quoniam memor fuit Domini in toto corde suo, dedit illi Deus gratiam in conspectu Salmanasar regis,
vulgate.1:14: et dedit illi potestatem quocumque vellet ire, habens libertatem quæcumque facere voluisset.
vulgate.1:15: Pergebat ergo ad omnes qui erant in captivitate, et monita salutis dabat eis.
vulgate.1:16: Cum autem venisset in Rages civitatem Medorum, et ex his quibus honoratus fuerat a rege, habuisset decem talenta argenti:
vulgate.1:17: et cum in multa turba generis sui Gabelum egentem videret, qui erat ex tribu ejus, sub chirographo dedit illi memoratum pondus argenti.
vulgate.1:18: Post multum vero temporis, mortuo Salmanasar rege, cum regnaret Sennacherib filius ejus pro eo, et filios Israël exosos haberet in conspectu suo,
vulgate.1:19: Tobias quotidie pergebat per omnem cognationem suam, et consolabatur eos, dividebatque unicuique, prout poterat, de facultatibus suis:
vulgate.1:20: esurientes alebat, nudisque vestimenta præbebat, et mortuis atque occisis sepulturam sollicitus exhibebat.
vulgate.1:21: Denique cum reversus esset rex Sennacherib, fugiens a Judæa plagam quam circa eum fecerat Deus propter blasphemiam suam, et iratus multos occideret ex filiis Israël, Tobias sepeliebat corpora eorum.
vulgate.1:22: At ubi nuntiatum est regi, jussit eum occidi, et tulit omnem substantiam ejus.
vulgate.1:23: Tobias vero cum filio suo et cum uxore suo fugiens, nudus latuit, quia multi diligebant eum.
vulgate.1:24: Post dies vero quadraginta quinque occiderunt regem filii ipsius,
vulgate.1:25: et reversus est Tobias in domum suam, omnisque facultas ejus restituta est ei.
vulgate.2:1: Post hæc vero, cum esset dies festus Domini, et factum esset prandium bonum in domo Tobiæ,
vulgate.2:2: dixit filio suo: Vade, et adduc aliquos de tribu nostra, timentes Deum, ut epulentur nobiscum.
vulgate.2:3: Cumque abiisset, reversus nuntiavit ei unum ex filiis Israël jugulatum jacere in platea. Statimque exiliens de accubitu suo, relinquens prandium, jejunus pervenit ad corpus:
vulgate.2:4: tollensque illud portavit ad domum suam occulte, ut dum sol occubuisset, caute sepeliret eum.
vulgate.2:5: Cumque occultasset corpus, manducavit panem cum luctu et tremore,
vulgate.2:6: memorans illum sermonem, quem dixit Dominus per Amos prophetam: Dies festi vestri convertentur in lamentationem et luctum.
vulgate.2:7: Cum vero sol occubuisset, abiit, et sepelivit eum.
vulgate.2:8: Arguebant autem eum omnes proximi ejus, dicentes: Jam hujus rei causa interfici jussus es, et vix effugisti mortis imperium, et iterum sepelis mortuos?
vulgate.2:9: Sed Tobias plus timens Deum quam regem, rapiebat corpora occisorum, et occultabat in domo sua, et mediis noctibus sepeliebat ea.
vulgate.2:10: Contigit autem ut quadam die fatigatus a sepultura, veniens in domum suam, jactasset se juxta parietem, et obdormisset,
vulgate.2:11: et ex nido hirundinum dormienti illi calida stercora inciderent super oculos ejus, fieretque cæcus.
vulgate.2:12: Hanc autem tentationem ideo permisit Dominus evenire illi, ut posteris daretur exemplum patientiæ ejus, sicut et sancti Job.
vulgate.2:13: Nam cum ab infantia sua semper Deum timuerit, et mandata ejus custodierit, non est contristatus contra Deum quod plaga cæcitatis evenerit ei,
vulgate.2:14: sed immobilis in Dei timore permansit, agens gratias Deo omnibus diebus vitæ suæ.
vulgate.2:15: Nam sicut beato Job insultabant reges, ita isti parentes et cognati ejus irridebant vitam ejus, dicentes:
vulgate.2:16: Ubi est spes tua, pro qua eleemosynas et sepulturas faciebas?
vulgate.2:17: Tobias vero increpabat eos, dicens: Nolite ita loqui:
vulgate.2:18: quoniam filii sanctorum sumus, et vitam illam expectamus, quam Deus daturus est his qui fidem suam numquam mutant ab eo.
vulgate.2:19: Anna vero uxor ejus ibat ad opus textrinum quotidie, et de labore manuum suarum victum quem consequi poterat, deferebat.
vulgate.2:20: Unde factum est ut hædum caprarum accipiens detulisset domi:
vulgate.2:21: cujus cum vocem balantis vir ejus audisset, dixit: Videte, ne forte furtivus sit: reddite eum dominis suis, quia non licet nobis aut edere ex furto aliquid, aut contingere.
vulgate.2:22: Ad hæc uxor ejus irata respondit: Manifeste vana facta est spes tua, et eleemosynæ tuæ modo apparuerunt.
vulgate.2:23: Atque his et aliis hujuscemodi verbis exprobrabat ei.
vulgate.3:1: Tunc Tobias ingemuit, et cœpit orare cum lacrimis,
vulgate.3:2: dicens: Justus es, Domine, et omnia judicia tua justa sunt, et omnes viæ tuæ, misericordia, et veritas, et judicium.
vulgate.3:3: Et nunc Domine, memor esto mei, et ne vindictam sumas de peccatis meis, neque reminiscaris delicta mea, vel parentum meorum.
vulgate.3:4: Quoniam non obedivimus præceptis tuis, ideo traditi sumus in direptionem, et captivitatem, et mortem, et in fabulam, et in improperium omnibus nationibus in quibus dispersisti nos.
vulgate.3:5: Et nunc Domine, magna judicia tua, quia non egimus secundum præcepta tua, et non ambulavimus sinceriter coram te.
vulgate.3:6: Et nunc Domine, secundum voluntatem tuam fac mecum, et præcipe in pace recipi spiritum meum: expedit enim mihi mori magis quam vivere.
vulgate.3:7: Eadem itaque die, contigit ut Sara filia Raguelis in Rages civitate Medorum et ipsa audiret improperium ab una ex ancillis patris sui,
vulgate.3:8: quoniam tradita fuerat septem viris, et dæmonium nomine Asmodæus occiderat eos, mox ut ingressi fuissent ad eam.
vulgate.3:9: Ergo cum pro culpa sua increparet puellam, respondit ei, dicens: Amplius ex te non videamus filium aut filiam super terram, interfectrix virorum tuorum.
vulgate.3:10: Numquid et occidere me vis, sicut jam occidisti septem viros? Ad hanc vocem perrexit in superius cubiculum domus suæ: et tribus diebus, et tribus noctibus non manducavit, neque bibit:
vulgate.3:11: sed in oratione persistens cum lacrimis deprecabatur Deum, ut ab isto improperio liberaret eam.
vulgate.3:12: Factum est autem die tertia, dum compleret orationem, benedicens Dominum
vulgate.3:13: dixit: Benedictum est nomen tuum, Deus patrum nostrorum: qui cum iratus fueris, misericordiam facies, et in tempore tribulationis peccata dimittis his qui invocant te.
vulgate.3:14: Ad te, Domine, faciem meam converto; ad te oculos meos dirigo.
vulgate.3:15: Peto, Domine, ut de vinculo improperii hujus absolvas me, aut certe desuper terram eripias me.
vulgate.3:16: Tu scis, Domine, quia numquam concupivi virum, et mundam servavi animam meam ab omni concupiscentia.
vulgate.3:17: Numquam cum ludentibus miscui me, neque cum his qui in levitate ambulant, participem me præbui.
vulgate.3:18: Virum autem cum timore tuo, non cum libidine mea, consensi suscipere.
vulgate.3:19: Et, aut ego indigna fui illis, aut illi forsitan me non fuerunt digni, quia forsitan viro alii conservasti me.
vulgate.3:20: Non est enim in hominis potestate consilium tuum.
vulgate.3:21: Hoc autem pro certo habet omnis qui te colit: quod vita ejus, si in probatione fuerit, coronabitur; si autem in tribulatione fuerit, liberabitur; et si in correptione fuerit, ad misericordiam tuam venire licebit.
vulgate.3:22: Non enim delectaris in perditionibus nostris: quia post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post lacrimationem et fletum, exultationem infundis.
vulgate.3:23: Sit nomen tuum, Deus Israël, benedictum in sæcula.
vulgate.3:24: In illo tempore exauditæ sunt preces amborum in conspectu gloriæ summi Dei:
vulgate.3:25: et missus est angelus Domini sanctus Raphaël ut curaret eos ambos, quorum uno tempore sunt orationes in conspectu Domini recitatæ.
vulgate.4:1: Igitur cum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri ut mori potuisset, vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum,
vulgate.4:2: dixitque ei: Audi, fili mi, verba oris mei, et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe.
vulgate.4:3: Cum acceperit Deus animam meam, corpus meum sepeli: et honorem habebis matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus:
vulgate.4:4: memor enim esse debes, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo.
vulgate.4:5: Cum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ, sepelias eam circa me.
vulgate.4:6: Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum: et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias, et prætermittas præcepta Domini Dei nostri.
vulgate.4:7: Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam, et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere: ita enim fiet ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini.
vulgate.4:9: Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue: si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude.
vulgate.4:10: Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurizas in die necessitatis:
vulgate.4:11: quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte liberat, et non patietur animam ire in tenebras.
vulgate.4:12: Fiducia magna erit coram summo Deo, eleemosyna omnibus facientibus eam.
vulgate.4:13: Attende tibi, fili mi, ab omni fornicatione, et præter uxorem tuam numquam patiaris crimen scire.
vulgate.4:14: Superbiam numquam in tuo sensu aut in tuo verbo dominari permittas: in ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio.
vulgate.4:15: Quicumque tibi aliquid operatus fuerit, statim ei mercedem restitue, et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat.
vulgate.4:16: Quod ab alio oderis fieri tibi, vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias.
vulgate.4:17: Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede, et de vestimentis tuis nudos tege.
vulgate.4:18: Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue, et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus.
vulgate.4:20: Omni tempore benedic Deum: et pete ab eo ut vias tuas dirigat, et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant.
vulgate.4:21: Indico etiam tibi, fili mi, dedisse me decem talenta argenti, dum adhuc infantulus esses, Gabelo, in Rages civitate Medorum, et chirographum ejus apud me habeo:
vulgate.4:22: et ideo perquire quomodo ad eum pervenias, et recipias ab eo supra memoratum pondus argenti, et restituas ei chirographum suum.
vulgate.4:23: Noli timere, fili mi: pauperem quidem vitam gerimus, sed multa bona habebimus si timuerimus Deum, et recesserimus ab omni peccato, et fecerimus bene.
vulgate.5:1: Tunc respondit Tobias patri suo, et dixit: Omnia quæcumque præcepisti mihi faciam, pater.
vulgate.5:2: Quomodo autem pecuniam hanc requiram, ignoro: ille me nescit, et ego eum ignoro: quod signum dabo ei? sed neque viam per quam pergatur illuc aliquando cognovi.
vulgate.5:3: Tunc pater suus respondit illi, et dixit: Chirographum quidem illius penes me habeo: quod dum illi ostenderis, statim restituet.
vulgate.5:4: Sed perge nunc, et inquire tibi aliquem fidelem virum, qui eat tecum salva mercede sua, ut dum adhuc vivo, recipias eam.
vulgate.5:5: Tunc egressus Tobias, invenit juvenem splendidum stantem præcinctum, et quasi paratum ad ambulandum.
vulgate.5:6: Et ignorans quod angelus Dei esset, salutavit eum, et dixit: Unde te habemus, bone juvenis?
vulgate.5:7: At ille respondit: Ex filiis Israël. Et Tobias dixit ei: Nosti viam quæ ducit in regionem Medorum?
vulgate.5:8: Cui respondit: Novi: et omnia itinera ejus frequenter ambulavi, et mansi apud Gabelum fratrem nostrum, qui moratur in Rages civitate Medorum, quæ posita est in monte Ecbatanis.
vulgate.5:9: Cui Tobias ait: Sustine me obsecro, donec hæc ipsa nuntiem patri meo.
vulgate.5:10: Tunc ingressus Tobias, indicavit universa hæc patri suo. Super quæ admiratus pater, rogavit ut introiret ad eum.
vulgate.5:11: Ingressus itaque salutavit eum, et dixit: Gaudium tibi sit semper.
vulgate.5:12: Et ait Tobias: Quale gaudium mihi erit, qui in tenebris sedeo, et lumen cæli non video?
vulgate.5:13: Cui ait juvenis: Forti animo esto: in proximo est ut a Deo cureris.
vulgate.5:14: Dixit itaque illi Tobias: Numquid poteris perducere filium meum ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum? et cum redieris, restituam tibi mercedem tuam.
vulgate.5:15: Et dixit ei angelus: Ego ducam, et reducam eum ad te.
vulgate.5:16: Cui Tobias respondit: Rogo te, indica mihi de qua domo aut de qua tribu es tu.
vulgate.5:17: Cui Raphaël angelus dixit: Genus quæris mercenarii, an ipsum mercenarium qui cum filio tuo eat?
vulgate.5:18: sed ne forte sollicitum te reddam, ego sum Azarias Ananiæ magni filius.
vulgate.5:19: Et Tobias respondit: Ex magno genere es tu. Sed peto ne irascaris quod voluerim cognoscere genus tuum.
vulgate.5:20: Dixit autem illi angelus: Ego sanum ducam, et sanum tibi reducam filium tuum.
vulgate.5:21: Respondens autem Tobias, ait: Bene ambuletis, et sit Deus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum.
vulgate.5:22: Tunc paratis omnibus quæ erant in via portanda, fecit Tobias vale patri suo et matri suæ, et ambulaverunt ambo simul.
vulgate.5:23: Cumque profecti essent, cœpit mater ejus flere, et dicere: Baculum senectutis nostræ tulisti, et transmisisti a nobis.
vulgate.5:24: Numquam fuisset ipsa pecunia, pro qua misisti eum:
vulgate.5:25: sufficiebat enim nobis paupertas nostra, ut divitias computaremus hoc, quod videbamus filium nostrum.
vulgate.5:26: Dixitque ei Tobias: Noli flere: salvus perveniet filius noster, et salvus revertetur ad nos, et oculi tui videbunt illum.
vulgate.5:27: Credo enim quod angelus Dei bonus comitetur ei, et bene disponat omnia quæ circa eum geruntur, ita ut cum gaudio revertatur ad nos.
vulgate.5:28: Ad hanc vocem cessavit mater ejus flere, et tacuit.
vulgate.6:1: Profectus est autem Tobias, et canis secutus est eum, et mansit prima mansione juxta fluvium Tigris.
vulgate.6:2: Et exivit ut lavaret pedes suos, et ecce piscis immanis exivit ad devorandum eum.
vulgate.6:3: Quem expavescens Tobias clamavit voce magna, dicens: Domine, invadit me.
vulgate.6:4: Et dixit ei angelus: Apprehende branchiam ejus, et trahe eum ad te. Quod cum fecisset, attraxit eum in siccum, et palpitare cœpit ante pedes ejus.
vulgate.6:5: Tunc dixit ei angelus: Exentera hunc piscem, et cor ejus, et fel, et jecur repone tibi: sunt enim hæc necessaria ad medicamenta utiliter.
vulgate.6:6: Quod cum fecisset, assavit carnes ejus, et secum tulerunt in via: cetera salierunt, quæ sufficerent eis, quousque pervenirent in Rages civitatem Medorum.
vulgate.6:7: Tunc interrogavit Tobias angelum, et dixit ei: Obsecro te, Azaria frater, ut dicas mihi quod remedium habebunt ista, quæ de pisce servare jussisti?
vulgate.6:8: Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Cordis ejus particulam si super carbones ponas, fumus ejus extricat omne genus dæmoniorum sive a viro, sive a muliere, ita ut ultra non accedat ad eos.
vulgate.6:9: Et fel valet ad ungendos oculos in quibus fuerit albugo, et sanabuntur.
vulgate.6:10: Et dixit ei Tobias: Ubi vis ut maneamus?
vulgate.6:11: Respondensque angelus, ait: Est hic Raguel nomine, vir propinquus de tribu tua, et hic habet filiam nomine Saram, sed neque masculum neque feminam ullam habet aliam præter eam.
vulgate.6:12: Tibi debetur omnis substantia ejus, et oportet eam te accipere conjugem.
vulgate.6:13: Pete ergo eam a patre ejus, et dabit tibi eam in uxorem.
vulgate.6:14: Tunc respondit Tobias, et dixit: Audio quia tradita est septem viris, et mortui sunt: sed et hoc audivi, quia dæmonium occidit illos.
vulgate.6:15: Timeo ergo, ne forte et mihi hæc eveniant: et cum sim unicus parentibus meis, deponam senectutem illorum cum tristitia ad inferos.
vulgate.6:16: Tunc angelus Raphaël dixit ei: Audi me, et ostendam tibi qui sunt, quibus prævalere potest dæmonium.
vulgate.6:17: Hi namque qui conjugium ita suscipiunt, ut Deum a se et a sua mente excludant, et suæ libidini ita vacent sicut equus et mulus quibus non est intellectus: habet potestatem dæmonium super eos.
vulgate.6:18: Tu autem cum acceperis eam, ingressus cubiculum, per tres dies continens esto ab ea, et nihil aliud nisi orationibus vacabis cum ea.
vulgate.6:19: Ipsa autem nocte, incenso jecore piscis, fugabitur dæmonium.
vulgate.6:20: Secunda vero nocte in copulatione sanctorum patriarcharum admitteris.
vulgate.6:21: Tertia autem nocte, benedictionem consequeris, ut filii ex vobis procreentur incolumes.
vulgate.6:22: Transacta autem tertia nocte, accipies virginem cum timore Domini, amore filiorum magis quam libidine ductus, ut in semine Abrahæ benedictionem in filiis consequaris.
vulgate.7:1: Ingressi sunt autem ad Raguelem, et suscepit eos Raguel cum gaudio.
vulgate.7:2: Intuensque Tobiam Raguel, dixit Annæ uxori suæ: Quam similis est juvenis iste consobrino meo!
vulgate.7:3: Et cum hæc dixisset, ait: Unde estis juvenes fratres nostri? At illi dixerunt: Ex tribu Nephthali sumus, ex captivitate Ninive.
vulgate.7:4: Dixitque illis Raguel: Nostis Tobiam fratrem meum? Qui dixerunt: Novimus.
vulgate.7:5: Cumque multa bona loqueretur de eo, dixit angelus ad Raguelem: Tobias, de quo interrogas, pater istius est.
vulgate.7:6: Et misit se Raguel, et cum lacrimis osculatus est eum, et plorans supra collum ejus
vulgate.7:7: dixit: Benedictio sit tibi, fili mi, quia boni et optimi viri filius es.
vulgate.7:8: Et Anna uxor ejus, et Sara ipsorum filia, lacrimatæ sunt.
vulgate.7:9: Postquam autem locuti sunt, præcepit Raguel occidi arietem, et parari convivium. Cumque hortaretur eos discumbere ad prandium,
vulgate.7:10: Tobias dixit: Hic ego hodie non manducabo neque bibam, nisi prius petitionem meam confirmes, et promittas mihi dare Saram filiam tuam.
vulgate.7:11: Quo audito verbo Raguel expavit, sciens quid evenerit illis septem viris qui ingressi sunt ad eam: et timere cœpit ne forte et hunc similiter contingeret. Et cum nutaret, et non daret petenti ullum responsum,
vulgate.7:12: dixit ei angelus: Noli timere dare eam isti, quoniam huic timenti Deum debetur conjux filia tua: propterea alius non potuit habere illam.
vulgate.7:13: Tunc dixit Raguel: Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas in conspectu suo admiserit.
vulgate.7:14: Et credo quoniam ideo fecit vos venire ad me, ut ista conjungeretur cognationi suæ secundum legem Moysi: et nunc noli dubium gerere quod tibi eam tradam.
vulgate.7:15: Et apprehendens dexteram filiæ suæ, dexteræ Tobiæ tradidit, dicens: Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob vobiscum sit, et ipse conjungat vos, impleatque benedictionem suam in vobis.
vulgate.7:16: Et accepta carta, fecerunt conscriptionem conjugii.
vulgate.7:17: Et post hæc epulati sunt, benedicentes Deum.
vulgate.7:18: Vocavitque Raguel ad se Annam uxorem suam, et præcepit ei ut præpararet alterum cubiculum.
vulgate.7:19: Et introduxit illuc Saram filiam suam, et lacrimata est.
vulgate.7:20: Dixitque ei: Forti animo esto, filia mea: Dominus cæli det tibi gaudium pro tædio quod perpessa es.
vulgate.8:1: Postquam vero cœnaverunt, introduxerunt juvenem ad eam.
vulgate.8:2: Recordatus itaque Tobias sermonum angeli, protulit de cassidili suo partem jecoris, posuitque eam super carbones vivos.
vulgate.8:3: Tunc Raphaël angelus apprehendit dæmonium, et religavit illud in deserto superioris Ægypti.
vulgate.8:4: Tunc hortatus est virginem Tobias, dixitque ei: Sara, exsurge, et deprecemur Deum hodie, et cras, et secundum cras: quia his tribus noctibus Deo jungimur; tertia autem transacta nocte, in nostro erimus conjugio.
vulgate.8:5: Filii quippe sanctorum sumus, et non possumus ita conjungi sicut gentes quæ ignorant Deum.
vulgate.8:6: Surgentes autem pariter, instanter orabant ambo simul, ut sanitas daretur eis.
vulgate.8:7: Dixitque Tobias: Domine Deus patrum nostrorum, benedicant te cæli et terræ, mareque et fontes, et flumina, et omnes creaturæ tuæ quæ in eis sunt.
vulgate.8:8: Tu fecisti Adam de limo terræ, dedistique ei adjutorium Hevam.
vulgate.8:9: Et nunc Domine, tu scis quia non luxuriæ causa accipio sororem meam conjugem, sed sola posteritatis dilectione, in qua benedicatur nomen tuum in sæcula sæculorum.
vulgate.8:10: Dixit quoque Sara: Miserere nobis Domine, miserere nobis, et consenescamus ambo pariter sani.
vulgate.8:11: Et factum est circa pullorum cantum, accersiri jussit Raguel servos suos, et abierunt cum eo pariter ut foderent sepulchrum.
vulgate.8:12: Dicebat enim: Ne forte simili modo evenerit ei, quo et ceteris illis septem viris qui sunt ingressi ad eam.
vulgate.8:13: Cumque parassent fossam, reversus Raguel ad uxorem suam, dixit ei:
vulgate.8:14: Mitte unam de ancillis tuis, et videat si mortuus est, ut sepeliam eum antequam illucescat dies.
vulgate.8:15: At illa misit unam ex ancillis suis. Quæ ingressa cubiculum, reperit eos salvos et incolumes, secum pariter dormientes.
vulgate.8:16: Et reversa nuntiavit bonum nuntium: et benedixerunt Dominum, Raguel videlicet et Anna uxor ejus,
vulgate.8:17: et dixerunt: Benedicimus te, Domine Deus Israël, quia non contigit quemadmodum putabamus.
vulgate.8:18: Fecisti enim nobiscum misericordiam tuam, et exclusisti a nobis inimicum persequentem nos.
vulgate.8:19: Misertus es autem duobus unicis. Fac eos, Domine, plenius benedicere te, et sacrificium tibi laudis tuæ et suæ sanitatis offerre, ut cognoscat universitas gentium quia tu es Deus solus in universa terra.
vulgate.8:20: Statimque præcepit servis suis Raguel ut replerent fossam quam fecerant priusquam elucesceret.
vulgate.8:21: Uxori autem suæ dixit ut instrueret convivium, et præpararet omnia quæ in cibos erant iter agentibus necessaria.
vulgate.8:22: Duas quoque pingues vaccas, et quatuor arietes, occidi fecit, et parari epulas omnibus vicinis suis, cunctisque amicis.
vulgate.8:23: Et adjuravit Raguel Tobiam ut duas hebdomadas moraretur apud se.
vulgate.8:24: De omnibus autem quæ possidebat Raguel, dimidiam partem dedit Tobiæ, et fecit scripturam, ut pars dimidia quæ supererat, post obitum eorum Tobiæ dominio deveniret.
vulgate.9:1: Tunc vocavit Tobias angelum ad se, quem quidem hominem existimabat, dixitque ei: Azaria frater, peto ut auscultes verba mea.
vulgate.9:2: Si meipsum tradam tibi servum, non ero condignus providentiæ tuæ:
vulgate.9:3: tamen obsecro te ut assumas tibi animalia sive servitia, et vadas ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum, reddasque ei chirographum suum, et recipias ab eo pecuniam, et roges eum venire ad nuptias meas.
vulgate.9:4: Scis enim ipse quoniam numerat pater meus dies, et si tardavero una die plus, contristatur anima ejus.
vulgate.9:5: Et certe vides quomodo adjuravit me Raguel, cujus adjuramentum spernere non possum.
vulgate.9:6: Tunc Raphaël assumens quatuor ex servis Raguelis, et duos camelos, in Rages civitatem Medorum perrexit: et inveniens Gabelum, reddidit ei chirographum suum, et recepit ab eo omnem pecuniam.
vulgate.9:7: Indicavitque ei de Tobia filio Tobiæ omnia quæ gesta sunt, fecitque eum secum venire ad nuptias.
vulgate.9:8: Cumque ingressus esset domum Raguelis, invenit Tobiam discumbentem: et exiliens, osculati sunt se invicem: et flevit Gabelus, benedixitque Deum,
vulgate.9:9: et dixit: Benedicat te Deus Israël, quia filius es optimi viri et justi, et timentis Deum, et eleemosynas facientis:
vulgate.9:10: et dicatur benedictio super uxorem tuam, et super parentes vestros,
vulgate.9:11: et videatis filios vestros, et filios filiorum vestrorum, usque in tertiam et quartam generationem: et sit semen vestrum benedictum a Deo Israël, qui regnat in sæcula sæculorum.
vulgate.9:12: Cumque omnes dixissent: Amen: accesserunt ad convivium: sed et cum timore Domini nuptiarum convivium exercebant.
vulgate.10:1: Cum vero moras faceret Tobias, causa nuptiarum, sollicitus erat pater ejus Tobias, dicens: Putas quare moratur filius meus, aut quare detentus est ibi?
vulgate.10:2: Putasne Gabelus mortuus est, et nemo reddet illi pecuniam?
vulgate.10:3: Cœpit autem contristari nimis ipse, et Anna uxor ejus cum eo: et cœperunt ambo simul flere, eo quod die statuto minime reverteretur filius eorum ad eos.
vulgate.10:4: Flebat igitur mater ejus irremediabilibus lacrimis, atque dicebat: Heu, heu me, fili mi! ut quid te misimus peregrinari, lumen oculorum nostrorum, baculum senectutis nostræ, solatium vitæ nostræ, spem posteritatis nostræ?
vulgate.10:5: omnia simul in te uno habentes, te non debuimus dimittere a nobis.
vulgate.10:6: Cui dicebat Tobias: Tace, et noli turbari: sanus est filius noster: satis fidelis est vir ille, cum quo misimus eum.
vulgate.10:7: Illa autem nullo modo consolari poterat, sed quotidie exiliens circumspiciebat, et circuibat vias omnes per quas spes remeandi videbatur, ut procul videret eum, si fieri posset, venientem.
vulgate.10:8: At vero Raguel dicebat ad generum suum: Mane hic, et ego mittam nuntium salutis de te ad Tobiam patrem tuum.
vulgate.10:9: Cui Tobias ait: Ego novi quia pater meus et mater mea modo dies computant, et cruciatur spiritus eorum in ipsis.
vulgate.10:10: Cumque verbis multis rogaret Raguel Tobiam, et ille eum nulla ratione vellet audire, tradidit ei Saram, et dimidiam partem omnis substantiæ suæ in pueris, in puellis, in pecudibus, in camelis, et in vaccis, et in pecunia multa: et salvum atque gaudentem dimisit eum a se,
vulgate.10:11: dicens: Angelus Domini sanctus sit in itinere vestro, perducatque vos incolumes, et inveniatis omnia recte circa parentes vestros, et videant oculi mei filios vestros priusquam moriar.
vulgate.10:12: Et apprehendentes parentes filiam suam, osculati sunt eam: et dimiserunt ire,
vulgate.10:13: monentes eam honorare soceros, diligere maritum, regere familiam, gubernare domum, et seipsam irreprehensibilem exhibere.
vulgate.11:1: Cumque reverterentur, pervenerunt ad Charan, quæ est in medio itinere contra Niniven, undecimo die.
vulgate.11:2: Dixitque angelus: Tobia frater, scis quemadmodum reliquisti patrem tuum.
vulgate.11:3: Si placet itaque tibi, præcedamus, et lento gradu sequantur iter nostrum familiæ, simul cum conjuge tua, et cum animalibus.
vulgate.11:4: Cumque hoc placuisset ut irent, dixit Raphaël ad Tobiam: Tolle tecum ex felle piscis: erit enim necessarium. Tulit itaque Tobias ex felle illo, et abierunt.
vulgate.11:5: Anna autem sedebat secus viam quotidie in supercilio montis, unde respicere poterat de longinquo.
vulgate.11:6: Et dum ex eodem loco specularetur adventum ejus, vidit a longe, et illico agnovit venientem filium suum: currensque nuntiavit viro suo, dicens: Ecce venit filius tuus.
vulgate.11:7: Dixitque Raphaël ad Tobiam: At ubi introieris domum tuam, statim adora Dominum Deum tuum: et gratias agens ei, accede ad patrem tuum, et osculare eum.
vulgate.11:8: Statimque lini super oculos ejus ex felle isto piscis, quod portas tecum: scias enim quoniam mox aperientur oculi ejus, et videbit pater tuus lumen cæli, et in aspectu tuo gaudebit.
vulgate.11:9: Tunc præcucurrit canis, qui simul fuerat in via: et quasi nuntius adveniens, blandimento suæ caudæ gaudebat.
vulgate.11:10: Et consurgens cæcus pater ejus, cœpit offendens pedibus currere: et data manu puero, occurrit obviam filio suo.
vulgate.11:11: Et suscipiens osculatus est eum cum uxore sua, et cœperunt ambo flere præ gaudio.
vulgate.11:12: Cumque adorassent Deum, et gratias egissent, consederunt.
vulgate.11:13: Tunc sumens Tobias de felle piscis, linivit oculos patris sui.
vulgate.11:14: Et sustinuit quasi dimidiam fere horam: et cœpit albugo ex oculis ejus, quasi membrana ovi, egredi.
vulgate.11:15: Quam apprehendens Tobias, traxit ab oculis ejus: statimque visum recepit.
vulgate.11:16: Et glorificabant Deum, ipse videlicet et uxor ejus, et omnes qui sciebant eum.
vulgate.11:17: Dicebatque Tobias: Benedico te, Domine Deus Israël, quia tu castigasti me, et tu salvasti me: et ecce ego video Tobiam filium meum.
vulgate.11:18: Ingressa est etiam post septem dies Sara uxor filii ejus et omnis familia sana, et pecora, et cameli, et pecunia multa uxoris; sed et illa pecunia, quam receperat a Gabelo.
vulgate.11:19: Et narravit parentibus suis omnia beneficia Dei, quæ fecisset circa eum per hominem qui eum duxerat.
vulgate.11:20: Veneruntque Achior et Nabath consobrini Tobiæ gaudentes ad Tobiam, et congratulantes ei de omnibus bonis quæ circa illum ostenderat Deus.
vulgate.11:21: Et per septem dies epulantes, omnes cum gaudio magno gavisi sunt.
vulgate.12:1: Tunc vocavit ad se Tobias filium suum, dixitque ei: Quid possumus dare viro isti sancto, qui venit tecum?
vulgate.12:2: Respondens Tobias, dixit patri suo: Pater, quam mercedem dabimus ei? aut quid dignum poterit esse beneficiis ejus?
vulgate.12:3: Me duxit et reduxit sanum, pecuniam a Gabelo ipse recepit, uxorem ipse me habere fecit, et dæmonium ab ea ipse compescuit: gaudium parentibus ejus fecit, meipsum a devoratione piscis eripuit, te quoque videre fecit lumen cæli, et bonis omnibus per eum repleti sumus. Quid illi ad hæc poterimus dignum dare?
vulgate.12:4: Sed peto te, pater mi, ut roges eum, si forte dignabitur medietatem de omnibus quæ allata sunt, sibi assumere.
vulgate.12:5: Et vocantes eum, pater scilicet et filius, tulerunt eum in partem: et rogare cœperunt ut dignaretur dimidiam partem omnium quæ attulerant acceptam habere.
vulgate.12:6: Tunc dixit eis occulte: Benedicite Deum cæli, et coram omnibus viventibus confitemini ei, quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam.
vulgate.12:7: Etenim sacramentum regis abscondere bonum est: opera autem Dei revelare et confiteri honorificum est.
vulgate.12:8: Bona est oratio cum jejunio, et eleemosyna magis quam thesauros auri recondere:
vulgate.12:9: quoniam eleemosyna a morte liberat, et ipsa est quæ purgat peccata, et facit invenire misericordiam et viam æternam.
vulgate.12:10: Qui autem faciunt peccatum et iniquitatem, hostes sunt animæ suæ.
vulgate.12:11: Manifesto ergo vobis veritatem, et non abscondam a vobis occultum sermonem.
vulgate.12:12: Quando orabas cum lacrimis, et sepeliebas mortuos, et derelinquebas prandium tuum, et mortuos abscondebas per diem in domo tua, et nocte sepeliebas eos, ego obtuli orationem tuam Domino.
vulgate.12:13: Et quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te.
vulgate.12:14: Et nunc misit me Dominus ut curarem te, et Saram uxorem filii tui a dæmonio liberarem.
vulgate.12:15: Ego enim sum Raphaël angelus, unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Dominum.
vulgate.12:16: Cumque hæc audissent, turbati sunt, et trementes ceciderunt super terram in faciem suam.
vulgate.12:17: Dixitque eis angelus: Pax vobis: nolite timere.
vulgate.12:18: Etenim cum essem vobiscum, per voluntatem Dei eram: ipsum benedicite, et cantate illi.
vulgate.12:19: Videbar quidem vobiscum manducare et bibere: sed ego cibo invisibili, et potu qui ab hominibus videri non potest, utor.
vulgate.12:20: Tempus est ergo ut revertar ad eum qui me misit: vos autem benedicite Deum, et narrate omnia mirabilia ejus.
vulgate.12:21: Et cum hæc dixisset, ab aspectu eorum ablatus est, et ultra eum videre non potuerunt.
vulgate.12:22: Tunc prostrati per horas tres in faciem, benedixerunt Deum: et exsurgentes narraverunt omnia mirabilia ejus.
vulgate.13:1: Aperiens autem Tobias senior os suum, benedixit Dominum, et dixit: Magnus es, Domine, in æternum, et in omnia sæcula regnum tuum:
vulgate.13:2: quoniam tu flagellas, et salvas; deducis ad inferos, et reducis: et non est qui effugiat manum tuam.
vulgate.13:3: Confitemini Domino, filii Israël, et in conspectu gentium laudate eum:
vulgate.13:4: quoniam ideo dispersit vos inter gentes quæ ignorant eum, ut vos enarretis mirabilia ejus, et faciatis scire eos quia non est alius deus omnipotens præter eum.
vulgate.13:5: Ipse castigavit nos propter iniquitates nostras, et ipse salvabit nos propter misericordiam suam.
vulgate.13:6: Aspicite ergo quæ fecit nobiscum, et cum timore et tremore confitemini illi: regemque sæculorum exaltate in operibus vestris.
vulgate.13:7: Ego autem in terra captivitatis meæ confitebor illi: quoniam ostendit majestatem suam in gentem peccatricem.
vulgate.13:8: Convertimini itaque peccatores, et facite justitiam coram Deo, credentes quod faciat vobiscum misericordiam suam.
vulgate.13:9: Ego autem et anima mea in eo lætabimur.
vulgate.13:10: Benedicite Dominum omnes electi ejus: agite dies lætitiæ, et confitemini illi.
vulgate.13:11: Jerusalem civitas Dei, castigavit te Dominus in operibus manuum tuarum.
vulgate.13:12: Confitere Domino in bonis tuis, et benedic Deum sæculorum: ut reædificet in te tabernaculum suum, et revocet ad te omnes captivos, et gaudeas in omnia sæcula sæculorum.
vulgate.13:13: Luce splendida fulgebis, et omnes fines terræ adorabunt te.
vulgate.13:14: Nationes ex longinquo ad te venient, et munera deferentes adorabunt in te Dominum, et terram tuam in sanctificationem habebunt:
vulgate.13:15: nomen enim magnum invocabunt in te.
vulgate.13:16: Maledicti erunt qui contempserint te, et condemnati erunt omnes qui blasphemaverint te: benedictique erunt qui ædificaverint te.
vulgate.13:17: Tu autem lætaberis in filiis tuis, quoniam omnes benedicentur, et congregabuntur ad Dominum.
vulgate.13:18: Beati omnes qui diligunt te, et qui gaudent super pace tua.
vulgate.13:19: Anima mea, benedic Dominum, quoniam liberavit Jerusalem civitatem suam a cunctis tribulationibus ejus Dominus Deus noster.
vulgate.13:20: Beatus ero si fuerint reliquiæ seminis mei ad videndam claritatem Jerusalem.
vulgate.13:21: Portæ Jerusalem ex sapphiro et smaragdo ædificabuntur, et ex lapide pretioso omnis circuitus murorum ejus.
vulgate.13:22: Ex lapide candido et mundo omnes plateæ ejus sternentur, et per vicos ejus alleluja cantabitur.
vulgate.13:23: Benedictus Dominus, qui exaltavit eam, et sit regnum ejus in sæcula sæculorum super eam. Amen.
vulgate.14:1: Et consummati sunt sermones Tobiæ. Et postquam illuminatus est Tobias, vixit annis quadraginta duobus, et vidit filios nepotum suorum.
vulgate.14:2: Completis itaque annis centum duobus, sepultus est honorifice in Ninive.
vulgate.14:3: Quinquaginta namque et sex annorum lumen oculorum amisit, sexagenarius vero recepit.
vulgate.14:4: Reliquum vero vitæ suæ in gaudio fuit, et cum bono profectu timoris Dei perrexit in pace.
vulgate.14:5: In hora autem mortis suæ vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum, et septem juvenes filios ejus nepotes suos, dixitque eis:
vulgate.14:6: Prope erit interitus Ninive: non enim excidit verbum Domini: et fratres nostri, qui dispersi sunt a terra Israël, revertentur ad eam.
vulgate.14:7: Omnis autem deserta terra ejus replebitur, et domus Dei, quæ in ea incensa est, iterum reædificabitur: ibique revertentur omnes timentes Deum,
vulgate.14:8: et relinquent gentes idola sua, et venient in Jerusalem, et inhabitabunt in ea:
vulgate.14:9: et gaudebunt in ea omnes reges terræ, adorantes regem Israël.
vulgate.14:10: Audite ergo, filii mei, patrem vestrum: servite Domino in veritate, et inquirite ut faciatis quæ placita sunt illi:
vulgate.14:11: et filiis vestris mandate ut faciant justitias et eleemosynas, ut sint memores Dei, et benedicant eum in omni tempore in veritate, et in tota virtute sua.
vulgate.14:12: Nunc ergo filii, audite me, et nolite manere hic: sed quacumque die sepelieritis matrem vestram circa me in uno sepulchro, ex eo dirigite gressus vestros ut exeatis hinc:
vulgate.14:13: video enim quia iniquitas ejus finem dabit ei.
vulgate.14:14: Factum est autem post obitum matris suæ, Tobias abscessit ex Ninive cum uxore sua, et filiis, et filiorum filiis, et reversus est ad soceros suos:
vulgate.14:15: invenitque eos incolumes in senectute bona: et curam eorum gessit, et ipse clausit oculos eorum: et omnem hæreditatem domus Raguelis ipse percepit: viditque quintam generationem, filios filiorum suorum.
vulgate.14:16: Et completis annis nonaginta novem in timore Domini, cum gaudio sepelierunt eum.
vulgate.14:17: Omnis autem cognatio ejus et omnis generatio ejus in bona vita et in sancta conversatione permansit, ita ut accepti essent tam Deo quam hominibus, et cunctis habitantibus in terra.

douay.1:1: Tobias of the tribe and city of Nephtali, (which is in the upper parts of Galilee above Naasson, beyond the way that leadeth to the west, having on the right hand the city of Sephet,)
douay.1:2: When he was made captive in the days of Salmanasar king of the Assyrians, even in his captivity, forsook not the way of truth,
douay.1:3: But every day gave all he could get to his brethren his fellow captives, that were of his kindred.
douay.1:4: And when he was younger than any of the tribe of Nephtali, yet did he no childish thing in his work.
douay.1:5: Moreover when all went to the golden calves which Jeroboam king of Israel had made, he alone fled the company of all,
douay.1:6: And went to Jerusalem to the temple of the Lord, and there adored the Lord God of Israel, offering faithfully all his firstfruits, and his tithes,
douay.1:7: So that in the third year he gave all his tithes to the proselytes, and strangers.
douay.1:8: These and such like things did he observe when but a boy according to the law of God.
douay.1:9: But when he was a man, he took to wife Anna of his own tribe, and had a son by her, whom he called after his own name,
douay.1:10: And from his infancy he taught him to fear God, and to abstain from all sin.
douay.1:11: And when by the captivity he with his wife and his son and all his tribe was come to the city of Ninive,
douay.1:12: (When all ate of the meats of the Gentiles) he kept his soul and never was defiled with their meats.
douay.1:13: And because he was mindful of the Lord with all his heart, God gave him favour in the sight of Salmanasar the king.
douay.1:14: And he gave him leave to go whithersoever he would, with liberty to do whatever he had a mind.
douay.1:15: He therefore went to all that were in captivity, and gave them wholesome admonitions.
douay.1:16: And when he was come to Rages a city of the Medes, and had ten talents of silver of that with which he had been honoured by the king:
douay.1:17: And when amongst a great multitude of his kindred, he saw Gabelus in want, who was one of his tribe, taking a note of his hand he gave him the aforesaid sum of money.
douay.1:18: But after a long time, Salmanasar the king being dead, when Sennacherib his son, who reigned in his place, had a hatred for the children of Israel:
douay.1:19: Tobias daily went among all his kindred and comforted them, and distributed to every one as he was able, out of his goods:
douay.1:20: He fed the hungry, and gave clothes to the naked, and was careful to bury the dead, and they that were slain.
douay.1:21: And when king Sennacherib was come back, fleeing from Judea by reason of the slaughter that God had made about him for his blasphemy, and being angry slew many of the children of Israel, Tobias buried their bodies.
douay.1:22: But when it was told the king, he commanded him to be slain, and took away all his substance.
douay.1:23: But Tobias fleeing naked away with his son and with his wife, lay concealed, for many loved him.
douay.1:24: But after forty-five days, the king was killed by his own sons.
douay.1:25: And Tobias returned to his house, and all his substance was restored to him.
douay.2:1: But after this, when there was a festival of the Lord, and a good dinner was prepared in Tobias's house,
douay.2:2: He said to his son: Go, and bring some of our tribe that fear God, to feast with us.
douay.2:3: And when he had gone, returning he told him, that one of the children of Israel lay slain in the street. And he forthwith leaped up from his place at the table, and left his dinner, and came fasting to the body.
douay.2:4: And taking it up carried it privately to his house, that after the sun was down, he might bury him cautiously.
douay.2:5: And when he had hid the body, he ate bread with mourning and fear,
douay.2:6: Remembering the word which the Lord spoke by Amos the prophet: Your festival days shall be turned into lamentation and mourning.
douay.2:7: So when the sun was down, he went and buried him.
douay.2:8: Now all his neighbours blamed him, saying: once already commandment was given for thee to be slain because of this matter, and thou didst scarce escape the sentence of death, and dost thou again bury the dead?
douay.2:9: But Tobias fearing God more than the king, carried off the bodies of them that were slain, and hid them in his house, and at midnight buried them.
douay.2:10: Now it happened one day that being wearied with burying, he came to his house, and cast himself down by the wall and slept,
douay.2:11: And as he was sleeping, hot dung out of a swallow's nest fell upon his eyes, and he was made blind.
douay.2:12: Now this trial the Lord therefore permitted to happen to him, that an example might be given to posterity of his patience, as also of holy Job.
douay.2:13: For whereas he had always feared God from his infancy, and kept his commandments, he repined not against God because the evil of blindness had befallen him,
douay.2:14: But continued immoveable in the fear of God, giving thanks to God all the days of his life.
douay.2:15: For as the kings insulted over holy Job: so his relations and kinsmen mocked at his life, saying:
douay.2:16: Where is thy hope, for which thou gavest alms, and buriedst the dead?
douay.2:17: But Tobias rebuked them, saying: Speak not so:
douay.2:18: For we are the children of saints, and look for that life which God will give to those that never change their faith from him.
douay.2:19: Now Anna his wife went daily to weaving work, and she brought home what she could get for their living by the labour of her hands.
douay.2:20: Whereby it came to pass, that she received a young kid, and brought it home:
douay.2:21: And when her husband heard it bleating, he said: Take heed, lest perhaps it be stolen: restore ye it to its owners, for it is not lawful for us either to eat or to touch any thing that cometh by theft.
douay.2:22: At these words his wife being angry answered: It is evident the hope is come to nothing, and thy alms now appear.
douay.2:23: And with these and other such like words, she upbraided him.
douay.3:1: Then Tobias sighed, and began to pray with tears,
douay.3:2: Saying, Thou art just, O Lord, and all thy judgments are just, and all thy ways mercy, and truth, and judgment:
douay.3:3: And now, O Lord, think of me, and take not revenge of my sins, neither remember my offences, nor those of my parents.
douay.3:4: For we have not obeyed thy commandments, therefore are we delivered to spoil and to captivity, and death, and are made a fable, and a reproach to all nations, amongst which thou hast scattered us.
douay.3:5: And now, O Lord, great are thy judgments, because we have not done according to thy precepts, and have not walked sincerely before thee.
douay.3:6: And now, O Lord, do with me according to thy will, and command my spirit to be received in peace: for it is better for me to die, than to live.
douay.3:7: Now it happened on the same day, that Sara daughter of Raguel, in Rages a city of the Medes, received a reproach from one of her father's servant maids,
douay.3:8: Because she had been given to seven husbands and a devil named Asmodeus had killed them, at their first going in unto her.
douay.3:9: So when she reproved the maid for her fault, she answered her, saying: May we never see son, or daughter of thee upon the earth, thou murderer of thy husbands.
douay.3:10: Wilt thou kill me also, as thou hast already killed seven husbands? At these words, she went into an upper chamber of her house: and for three days and three nights did neither eat nor drink:
douay.3:11: But continuing in prayer with tears besought God, that he would deliver her from this reproach.
douay.3:12: And it came to pass on the third day when she was making an end of her prayer, blessing the Lord,
douay.3:13: She said: Blessed is thy name, O God of our fathers, who when thou hast been angry, wilt shew mercy, and in the time of tribulation forgivest the sins of them that call upon thee.
douay.3:14: To thee, O Lord, I turn my face, to thee I direct my eyes.
douay.3:15: I beg, O Lord, that thou loose me from the bond of this reproach, or else take me away from the earth.
douay.3:16: Thou knowest, O Lord, that I never coveted a husband, and have kept my soul clean from all lust.
douay.3:17: Never have I joined myself with them that play: neither have I made myself partaker with them that walk in lightness.
douay.3:18: But a husband I consented to take, with thy fear, not with my lust.
douay.3:19: And either I was unworthy of them, or they perhaps were not worthy of me: because perhaps thou hast kept me for another man,
douay.3:20: For thy counsel is not in man's power.
douay.3:21: But this every one is sure of that worshippeth thee, that his life, if it be under trial, shall be crowned and if it be under tribulation, it shall be delivered: and if it be under correction, it shall be allowed to come to thy mercy.
douay.3:22: For thou art not delighted in our being lost, because after a storm thou makest a calm, and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness.
douay.3:23: Be thy name, O God of Israel, blessed for ever,
douay.3:24: At that time the prayers of them both were heard in the sight of the glory of the most high God:
douay.3:25: And the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael was sent to heal them both, whose prayers at one time were rehearsed in the sight of the Lord.
douay.4:1: Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard that he might die, he called to him Tobias his son,
douay.4:2: And said to him: Hear, my son, the words of my mouth, and lay them as a foundation in thy heart.
douay.4:3: When God shall take my soul, thou shalt bury my body: and thou shalt honour thy mother all the days of her life:
douay.4:4: For thou must be mindful what and how great perils she suffered for thee in her womb.
douay.4:5: And when she also shall have ended the time of her life, bury her by me.
douay.4:6: And all the days of thy life have God in thy mind: and take heed thou never consent to sin, nor transgress the commandments of the Lord our God.
douay.4:7: Give alms out of thy substance, and turn not away thy face from any poor person: for so it shall come to pass that the face of the Lord shall not be turned from thee.
douay.4:8: According to thy ability be merciful.
douay.4:9: If thou have much give abundantly: if thou have little, take care even so to bestow willingly a little.
douay.4:10: For thus thou storest up to thyself a good reward for the day of necessity.
douay.4:11: For alms deliver from all sin, and from death, and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness.
douay.4:12: Alms shall be a great confidence before the most high God, to all them that give it.
douay.4:13: Take heed to keep thyself, my son, from all fornication, and beside thy wife never endure to know a crime.
douay.4:14: Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind, or in thy words: for from it all perdition took its beginning.
douay.4:15: If any man hath done any work for thee, immediately pay him his hire, and let not the wages of thy hired servant stay with thee at all.
douay.4:16: See thou never do to another what thou wouldst hate to have done to thee by another.
douay.4:17: Eat thy bread with the hungry and the needy, and with thy garments cover the naked,
douay.4:18: Lay out thy bread, and thy wine upon the burial of a just man, and do not eat and drink thereof with the wicked.
douay.4:19: Seek counsel always of a wise man.
douay.4:20: Bless God at all times: and desire of him to direct thy ways, and that all thy counsels may abide in him.
douay.4:21: I tell thee also, my son, that I lent ten talents of silver, while thou wast yet a child, to Gabelus, in Rages a city of the Medes, and I have a note of his hand with me:
douay.4:22: Now therefore inquire how thou mayst go to him, and receive of him the foresaid sum of money, and restore to him the note of his hand.
douay.4:23: Fear not, my son: we lead indeed a poor life, but we shall have many good things if we fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is good.
douay.5:1: Then Tobias answered his father, and said: I will do all things, father, which thou hast commanded me.
douay.5:2: But how I shall get this money, I cannot tell; he knoweth not me, and I know not him: what token shall I give him? nor did I ever know the way which leadeth thither.
douay.5:3: Then his father answered him, and said: I have a note of his hand with me, which when thou shalt shew him, he will presently pay it.
douay.5:4: But go now, and seek thee out some faithful man, to go with thee for his hire: that thou mayst receive it, while I yet live.
douay.5:5: Then Tobias going forth, found a beautiful young man, standing girded, and as it were ready to walk.
douay.5:6: And not knowing that he was an angel of God, he saluted him, and said: From whence art thou, good young man?
douay.5:7: But he answered: Of the children of Israel. And Tobias said to him: Knowest thou the way that leadeth to the country of the Medes?
douay.5:8: And he answered: I know it: and I have often walked through all the ways thereof, and I have abode with Gabelus our brother, who dwelleth at Rages a city of the Medes, which is situate in the mount of Ecbatana.
douay.5:9: And Tobias said to him: Stay for me, I beseech thee, till I tell these same things to my father.
douay.5:10: Then Tobias going in told all these things to his father. Upon which his father being in admiration, desired that he would come in unto him.
douay.5:11: So going in he saluted him, and said: Joy be to thee always.
douay.5:12: And Tobias said: What manner of joy shall be to me, who sit in darkness and see not the light of heaven?
douay.5:13: And the young man said to him: Be of good courage, thy cure from God is at hand.
douay.5:14: And Tobias said to him: Canst thou conduct my son to Gabelus at Rages, a city of the Medes? and when thou shalt return, I will pay thee thy hire.
douay.5:15: And the angel said to him: I will conduct him thither, and bring him back to thee.
douay.5:16: And Tobias said to him: I pray thee, tell me, of what family, or what tribe art thou?
douay.5:17: And Raphael the angel answered: Dost thou seek the family of him thou hirest, or the hired servant himself to go with thy son?
douay.5:18: But lest I should make thee uneasy, I am Azarias the son of the great Ananias.
douay.5:19: And Tobias answered: Thou art of a great family. But I pray thee be not angry that I desired to know thy family.
douay.5:20: And the angel said to him: I will lead thy son safe, and bring him to thee again safe.
douay.5:21: And Tobias answering, said: May you have a good journey, and God be with you in your way, and his angel accompany you.
douay.5:22: Then all things being ready, that were to be carried in their journey, Tobias bade his father and his mother farewell, and they set out both together.
douay.5:23: And when they were departed, his mother began to weep, and to say: Thou hast taken the staff of our old age, and sent him away from us.
douay.5:24: I wish the money for which thou hast sent him, had never been.
douay.5:25: For our poverty was sufficient for us, that we might account it as riches, that we saw our son.
douay.5:26: And Tobias said to her: Weep not, our son will arrive thither safe, and will return safe to us, and thy eyes shall see him.
douay.5:27: For I believe that the good angel of God doth accompany him, and doth order all things well that are done about him, so that he shall return to us with joy.
douay.5:28: At these words his mother ceased weeping, and held her peace.
douay.6:1: And Tobias went forward, and the dog followed him, and he lodged the first night by the river of Tigris.
douay.6:2: And he went out to wash his feet, and behold a monstrous fish came up to devour him.
douay.6:3: And Tobias being afraid of him, cried out with a loud voice, saying: Sir, he cometh upon me.
douay.6:4: And the angel said to him: Take him by the gill, and draw him to thee. And when he had done so, he drew him out upon the land, and he began to pant before his feet.
douay.6:5: Then the angel said to him: Take out the entrails of this fish, and lay up his heart, and his gall, and his liver for thee: for these are necessary for useful medicines.
douay.6:6: And when he had done so, he roasted the flesh thereof, and they took it with them in the way: the rest they salted as much as might serve them, till they came to Rages the city of the Medes.
douay.6:7: Then Tobias asked the angel, and said to him: I beseech thee, brother Azarias, tell me what remedies are these things good for, which thou hast bid me keep of the fish?
douay.6:8: And the angel, answering, said to him: If thou put a little piece of its heart upon coals, the smoke thereof driveth away all kind of devils, either from man or from woman, so that they come no more to them.
douay.6:9: And the gall is good for anointing the eyes, in which there is a white speck, and they shall be cured.
douay.6:10: And Tobias said to him: Where wilt thou that we lodge?
douay.6:11: And the angel answering, said: Here is one whose name is Raguel, a near kinsman of thy tribe, and he hath a daughter named Sara, but he hath no son nor any other daughter beside her.
douay.6:12: All his substance is due to thee, and thou must take her to wife.
douay.6:13: Ask her therefore of her father, and he will give her thee to wife.
douay.6:14: Then Tobias answered, and said: I hear that she hath been given to seven husbands, and they all died: moreover I have heard, that a devil killed them.
douay.6:15: Now I am afraid, lest the same thing should happen to me also: and whereas I am the only child of my parents, I should bring down their old age with sorrow to hell.
douay.6:16: Then the angel Raphael said to him: Hear me, and I will shew thee who they are, over whom the devil can prevail.
douay.6:17: For they who in such manner receive matrimony, as to shut out God from themselves, and from their mind, and to give themselves to their lust, as the horse and mule, which have not understanding, over them the devil hath power.
douay.6:18: But thou when thou shalt take her, go into the chamber, and for three days keep thyself continent from her, and give thyself to nothing else but to prayers with her.
douay.6:19: And on that night lay the liver of the fish on the fire, and the devil shall be driven away.
douay.6:20: But the second night thou shalt be admitted into the society of the holy Patriarchs.
douay.6:21: And the third night thou shalt obtain a blessing that sound children may be born of you.
douay.6:22: And when the third night is past, thou shalt take the virgin with the fear of the Lord, moved rather for love of children than for lust, that in the seed of Abraham thou mayst obtain a blessing in children.
douay.7:1: And they went in to Raguel, and Raguel received them with joy.
douay.7:2: And Raguel looking upon Tobias, said to Anna his wife: How like is this young man to my cousin?
douay.7:3: And when he had spoken these words, he said: Whence are ye young men our brethren?
douay.7:4: But they said: We are of the tribe of Nephtali, of the captivity of Ninive.
douay.7:5: And Raguel said to them: Do you know Tobias my brother? And they said: We know him.
douay.7:6: And when he was speaking many good things of him, the angel said to Raguel: Tobias concerning whom thou inquirest is this young man's father.
douay.7:7: And Raguel went to him, and kissed him with tears and weeping upon his neck, said: A blessing be upon thee, my son, because thou art the son of a good and most virtuous man.
douay.7:8: And Anna his wife, and Sara their daughter wept.
douay.7:9: And after they had spoken, Raguel commanded a sheep to be killed, and a feast to be prepared. And when he desired them to sit down to dinner,
douay.7:10: Tobias said: I will not eat nor drink here this day, unless thou first grant me my petition, and promise to give me Sara thy daughter.
douay.7:11: Now when Raguel heard this he was afraid, knowing what had happened to those seven husbands, that went in unto her: and he began to fear lest it might happen to him also in like manner: and as he was in suspense, and gave no answer to his petition,
douay.7:12: The angel said to him: Be not afraid to give her to this man, for to him who feareth God is thy daughter due to be his wife: therefore another could not have her.
douay.7:13: Then Raguel said: I doubt not but God hath regarded my prayers and tears in his sight.
douay.7:14: And I believe he hath therefore made you come to me, that this maid might be married to one of her own kindred, according to the law of Moses: and now doubt not but I will give her to thee.
douay.7:15: And taking the right hand of his daughter, he gave it into the right hand of Tobias, saying: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you, and may he join you together, and fulfil his blessing in you.
douay.7:16: And taking paper they made a writing of the marriage.
douay.7:17: And afterwards they made merry, blessing God.
douay.7:18: And Raguel called to him Anna his wife, and bade her to prepare another chamber.
douay.7:19: And she brought Sara her daughter in thither, and she wept.
douay.7:20: And she said to her: Be of good cheer, my daughter: the Lord of heaven give thee joy for the trouble thou hast undergone.
douay.8:1: And after they had supped, they brought in the young man to her.
douay.8:2: And Tobias remembering the angel's word, took out of his bag part of the liver, and laid it upon burning coals.
douay.8:3: Then the angel Raphael took the devil, and bound him in the desert of upper Egypt.
douay.8:4: Then Tobias exhorted the virgin, and said to her: Sara, arise, and let us pray to God to day, and to morrow, and the next day: because for these three nights we are joined to God: and when the third night is over, we will be in our own wedlock.
douay.8:5: For we are the children of saints, and we must not be joined together like heathens that know not God.
douay.8:6: So they both arose, and prayed earnestly both together that health might be given them.
douay.8:7: And Tobias said: Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens and the earth, and the sea, and the fountains, and the rivers, and all thy creatures that are in them, bless thee.
douay.8:8: Thou madest Adam of the slime of the earth, and gavest him Eve for a helper.
douay.8:9: And now, Lord, thou knowest, that not for fleshly lust do I take my sister to wife, but only for the love of posterity, in which thy name may be blessed for ever and ever.
douay.8:10: Sara also said: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, and let us grow old both together in health.
douay.8:11: And it came to pass about the cockcrowing, Raguel ordered his servants to be called for, and they went with him together to dig a grave.
douay.8:12: For he said: Lest perhaps it may have happened to him, in like manner as it did to the other seven husbands, that went in unto her.
douay.8:13: And when they had prepared the pit, Raguel went back to his wife, and said to her:
douay.8:14: Send one of thy maids, and let her see if he be dead, that I may bury him before it be day.
douay.8:15: So she sent one of her maidservants, who went into the chamber, and found them safe and sound, sleeping both together.
douay.8:16: And returning she brought the good news: and Raguel and Anna his wife blessed the Lord,
douay.8:17: And said: We bless thee, O Lord God of Israel, because it hath not happened as we suspected.
douay.8:18: For thou hast shewn thy mercy to us, and hast shut out from us the enemy that persecuted us.
douay.8:19: And thou hast taken pity upon two only children. Make them, O Lord, bless thee more fully: and to offer up to thee a sacrifice of thy praise, and of their health, that all nations may know, that thou alone art God in all the earth.
douay.8:20: And immediately Raguel commanded his servants, to fill up the pit they had made, before it was day.
douay.8:21: And he spoke to his wife to make ready a feast, and prepare all kind of provisions that are necessary for such as go a journey.
douay.8:22: He caused also two fat kine, and four wethers to be killed, and a banquet to be prepared for all his neighbours, and all his friends.
douay.8:23: And Raguel adjured Tobias, to abide with him two weeks.
douay.8:24: And of all things which Raguel possessed, he gave one half to Tobias, and made a writing, that the half that remained should after their decease come also to Tobias.
douay.9:1: Then Tobias called the angel to him, whom he took to be a man, and said to him: Brother Azarias, I pray thee hearken to my words:
douay.9:2: If I should give myself to be thy servant I should not make a worthy return for thy care.
douay.9:3: However, I beseech thee, to take with thee beasts and servants, and to go to Gabelus to Rages the city of the Medes: and to restore to him his note of hand, and receive of him the money, and desire him to come to my wedding.
douay.9:4: For thou knowest that my father numbereth the days: and if I stay one day more, his soul will be afflicted.
douay.9:5: And indeed thou seest how Raguel hath adjured me, whose adjuring I cannot despise.
douay.9:6: Then Raphael took four of Raguel's servants, and two camels, and went to Rages the city of the Medes: and finding Gabelus, gave him his note of hand, and received of him all the money.
douay.9:7: And he told him concerning Tobias the son of Tobias, all that had been done: and made him come with him to the wedding.
douay.9:8: And when he was come into Raguel's house he found Tobias sitting at the table: and he leaped up, and they kissed each other: and Gabelus wept, and blessed God,
douay.9:9: And said: The God of Israel bless thee, because thou art the son of a very good and just man, and that feareth God, and doth almsdeeds:
douay.9:10: And may a blessing come upon thy wife and upon your parents.
douay.9:11: And may you see your children, and your children's children, unto the third and fourth generation: and may your seed be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigneth for ever and ever.
douay.9:12: And when all had said, Amen, they went to the feast: but the marriage feast they celebrated also with the fear of the Lord.
douay.10:1: But as Tobias made longer stay upon occasion of the marriage, Tobias his father was solicitous, saying: Why thinkest thou doth my son tarry, or why is he detained there?
douay.10:2: Is Gabelus dead, thinkest thou, and no man will pay him the money?
douay.10:3: And he began to be exceeding sad, both he and Anna his wife with him: and they began both to weep together, because their son did not return to them on the day appointed.
douay.10:4: But his mother wept and was quite disconsolate, and said: Woe, woe is me, my son; why did we send thee to go to a strange country, the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life, the hope of our posterity?
douay.10:5: We having all things together in thee alone, ought not to have let thee go from us.
douay.10:6: And Tobias said to her: Hold thy peace, and be not troubled, our son is safe: that man with whom we sent him is very trusty.
douay.10:7: But she could by no means be comforted, but daily running out looked round about, and went into all the ways by which there seemed any hope he might return, that she might if possible see him coming afar off.
douay.10:8: But Raguel said to his son in law: Stay here, and I will send a messenger to Tobias thy father, that thou art in health.
douay.10:9: And Tobias said to him: I know that my father and mother now count the days, and their spirit is grievously afflicted within them.
douay.10:10: And when Raguel had pressed Tobias with many words, and he by no means would hearken to him, he delivered Sara unto him, and half of all his substance in menservants, and womenservants, in cattle, in camels, and in kine, and in much money, and sent him away safe and joyful from him,
douay.10:11: Saying: The holy angel of the Lord be with you in your journey, and bring you through safe, and that you may find all things well about your parents, and my eyes may see your children before I die.
douay.10:12: And the parents taking their daughter kissed her, and let her go:
douay.10:13: Admonishing her to honour her father and mother in law, to love her husband, to take care of the family, to govern the house, and to behave herself irreprehensibly.
douay.11:1: And as they were returning they came to Charan, which is in the midway to Ninive, the eleventh day.
douay.11:2: And the angel said: Brother Tobias, thou knowest how thou didst leave thy father.
douay.11:3: If it please thee therefore, let us go before, and let the family follow softly after us, together with thy wife, and with the beasts.
douay.11:4: And as this their going pleased him, Raphael said to Tobias: Take with thee of the gall of the fish, for it will be necessary. So Tobias took some of that gall and departed.
douay.11:5: But Anna sat beside the way daily, on the top of a hill, from whence she might see afar off.
douay.11:6: And while she watched his coming from that place, she saw him afar off, and presently perceived it was her son coming: and returning she told her husband, saying: Behold thy son cometh.
douay.11:7: And Raphael said to Tobias: As soon as thou shalt come into thy house, forthwith adore the Lord thy God: and giving thanks to him, go to thy father, and kiss him.
douay.11:8: And immediately anoint his eyes with this gall of the fish, which thou carriest with thee. For be assured that his eyes shall be presently opened, and thy father shall see the light of heaven, and shall rejoice in the sight of thee.
douay.11:9: Then the dog, which had been with them in the way, ran before, and coming as if he had brought the news, shewed his joy by his fawning and wagging his tail.
douay.11:10: And his father that was blind, rising up, began to run stumbling with his feet: and giving a servant his hand, went to meet his son.
douay.11:11: And receiving him kissed him, as did also his wife, and they began to weep for joy.
douay.11:12: And when they had adored God, and given him thanks, they sat down together.
douay.11:13: Then Tobias taking of the gall of the fish, anointed his father's eyes.
douay.11:14: And he stayed about half an hour: and a white skin began to come out of his eyes, like the skin of an egg.
douay.11:15: And Tobias took hold of it, and drew it from his eyes, and recovered his sight.
douay.11:16: And they glorified God, both he and his wife and all that knew him.
douay.11:17: And Tobias said: I bless thee, O Lord God of Israel, because thou hast chastised me, and thou hast saved me and behold I see Tobias my son.
douay.11:18: And after seven days Sara his son's wife and all the family arrived safe, and the cattle, and the camels, and an abundance of money of his wife's: and that money also which he had received of Gabelus,
douay.11:19: And he told his parents all the benefits of God, which he had done to him by the man that conducted him.
douay.11:20: And Achior and Nabath the kinsmen of Tobias came, rejoicing for Tobias, and congratulating with him for all the good things that God had done for him.
douay.11:21: And for seven days they feasted and rejoiced all with great joy.
douay.12:1: Then Tobias called to him his son and said to him: What can we give to this holy man, that is come with thee?
douay.12:2: Tobias answering, said to his father: Father, what wages shall we give him? or what can be worthy of his benefits?
douay.12:3: He conducted me and brought me safe again, he received the money of Gabelus, he caused me to have my wife, and he chased from her the evil spirit, he gave joy to her parents, myself he delivered from being devoured by the fish, thee also he hath made to see the light of heaven, and we are filled with all good things through him. What can we give him sufficient for these things?
douay.12:4: But I beseech thee, my father, to desire him, that he would vouchsafe to accept of one half of all things that have been brought.
douay.12:5: So the father and the son calling him, took him aside: and began to desire him that he would vouchsafe to accept of half of all things that they had brought,
douay.12:6: Then he said to them secretly, Bless ye the God of heaven, give glory to him in the sight of all that live, because he hath shewn his mercy to you.
douay.12:7: For it is good to hide the secret of a king: to reveal and confess the works of God.
douay.12:8: Prayer is good with fasting and alms more than to lay up treasures of gold.
douay.12:9: For alms delivereth from death, and the same is that which purgeth away sins, and maketh to find mercy and life everlasting.
douay.12:10: But they that commit sin and iniquity, are enemies to their own soul.
douay.12:11: I discover then the truth unto you, and I will not hide the secret from you.
douay.12:12: When thou didst pray with tears, and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner, and hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord.
douay.12:13: And because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee.
douay.12:14: And now the Lord hath sent me to heal thee, and to deliver Sara thy son's wife from the devil.
douay.12:15: For I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord.
douay.12:16: And when they had heard these things, they were troubled, and being seized with fear they fell upon the ground on their face.
douay.12:17: And the angel said to them: Peace be to you, fear not.
douay.12:18: For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God: bless ye him, and sing praises to him.
douay.12:19: I seemed indeed to eat and to drink with you but I use an invisible meat and drink, which cannot be seen by men.
douay.12:20: It is time therefore that I return to him that sent me: but bless ye God, and publish all his wonderful works.
douay.12:21: And when he had said these things, he was taken from their sight, and they could see him no more.
douay.12:22: Then they lying prostrate for three hours upon their face, blessed God, and rising up, they told all his wonderful works.
douay.13:1: And Tobias the elder opening his mouth, blessed the Lord, and said: Thou art great O Lord, for ever, and thy kingdom is unto all ages.
douay.13:2: For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: and there is none that can escape thy hand.
douay.13:3: Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:
douay.13:4: Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, that you may declare his wonderful works, and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him.
douay.13:5: He hath chastised us for our iniquities: and he will save us for his own mercy.
douay.13:6: See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.
douay.13:7: As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation,
douay.13:8: Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, believing that he will shew his mercy to you.
douay.13:9: And I and my soul will rejoice in him.
douay.13:10: Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, keep days of joy, and give glory to him.
douay.13:11: Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord hath chastised thee for the works of thy hands.
douay.13:12: Give glory to the Lord for thy good things, and bless the God eternal that he may rebuild his tabernacle in thee, and may call back all the captives to thee, and thou mayst rejoice for ever and ever.
douay.13:13: Thou shalt shine with a glorious light: and all the ends of the earth shall worship thee,
douay.13:14: Nations from afar shall come to thee: and shall bring gifts, and shall adore the Lord in thee, and shall esteem thy land as holy.
douay.13:15: For they shall call upon the great name in thee,
douay.13:16: They shall be cursed that shall despise thee: and they shall be condemned that shall blaspheme thee: and blessed shall they be that shall build thee up,
douay.13:17: But thou shalt rejoice in thy children, because they shall all be blessed, and shall be gathered together to the Lord.
douay.13:18: Blessed are all they that love thee, and that rejoice in thy peace,
douay.13:19: My soul, bless thou the Lord, because the Lord our God hath delivered Jerusalem his city from all her troubles.
douay.13:20: Happy shall I be if there shall remain of my seed, to see the glory of Jerusalem.
douay.13:21: The gates of Jerusalem shall be built of sapphire, and of emerald, and all the walls thereof round about of precious stones.
douay.13:22: All its streets shall be paved with white and clean stones: and Alleluia shall be sung in its streets,
douay.13:23: Blessed be the Lord, who hath exalted it, and may he reign over it for ever and ever, Amen.
douay.14:1: And the words of Tobias were ended. And after Tobias was restored to his sight, he lived two and forty years, and saw the children of his grandchildren.
douay.14:2: And after he had lived a hundred and two years, he was buried honorably in Ninive.
douay.14:3: For he was six and fifty years old when he lost the sight of his eyes, and sixty when he recovered it again.
douay.14:4: And the rest of his life was in joy, and with great increase of the fear of God he departed in peace.
douay.14:5: And at the hour of his death he called unto him his son Tobias and his children, seven young men, his grandsons, and said to them:
douay.14:6: The destruction of Ninive is at hand: for the word of the Lord must be fulfilled: and our brethren, that are scattered abroad from the land of Israel, shall return to it.
douay.14:7: And all the land thereof that is desert shall be filled with people, and the house of God which is burnt in it, shall again be rebuilt: and all that fear God shall return thither.
douay.14:8: And the Gentiles shall leave their idols, and shall come into Jerusalem, and shall dwell in it.
douay.14:9: And all the kings of the earth shall rejoice in it, adoring the King of Israel.
douay.14:10: Hearken therefore, my children, to your father: serve the Lord in truth, and seek to do the things that please him:
douay.14:11: And command your children that they do justice and almsdeeds, and that they be mindful of God, and bless him at all times in truth, and with all their power.
douay.14:12: And now, children, hear me, and do not stay here: but as soon as you shall bury your mother by me in one sepulchre, without delay direct your steps to depart hence:
douay.14:13: For I see that its iniquity will bring it to destruction.
douay.14:14: And it came to pass that after the death of his mother, Tobias departed out of Ninive with his wife, and children, and children's children, and returned to his father and mother in law.
douay.14:15: And he found them in health in a good old age: and he took care of them, and he closed their eyes: and all the inheritance of Raguel's house came to him: and he saw his children's children to the fifth generation.
douay.14:16: And after he had lived ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, with joy they buried him.
douay.14:17: And all his kindred, and all his generation continued in good life, and in holy conversation, so that they were acceptable both to God, and to men, and to all that dwelt in the land.
